# Even stronger teachers can teach the wrong thing: evidence, compatibility, and preserving success

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/post-training/teacher-and-context.md) · English

Updated 2026-10-27 · 47 topic entries / 6 representative comparisons

Teacher value is more than aggregate score. OPSD changes training visibility, MOPD and token routing organize multiple teachers, CSD aligns probability events, SPOD protects successful student actions, and VAD isolates corrections attributable to visual evidence. Verify these constraints independently before imitation.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Mechanism comparison {#comparison}

Axes: Teacher source: a privileged same-weight view or independent domain experts · Combination granularity: domains, token routing, and successful action protection · Comparable interfaces: shared vocabulary coordinates or common text events · Attribution: privileged evidence, language priors, and existing student skills

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Check whether teacher signals describe the same event before mixing

MOPD and token routing can mix teachers but differ in domain-level and per-position selection. With different tokenizers, CSD first aligns decoded text events rather than mixing coordinates directly. OPSD can use the same model with extra conditions instead of adding independent experts.

Sources: [MOPD](../../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en.md) · [Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.21234-token-teacher-selection/README-en.md) · [CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer](../../../../post-training/2610.28895-csd/README-en.md) · [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md)

### Teacher corrections should be examined rather than accepted wholesale

SPOD protects specific successful actions the teacher disfavors, not whole successful episodes. VAD asks whether a privileged correction comes from visual evidence or shared language bias. Student success and evidence attribution are separate checks even when the teacher scores higher overall.

Sources: [Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.25034-spod/README-en.md) · [VAD](../../../../post-training/2607.28590-vad/README-en.md) · [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why isn't same-weight OPSD just letting the student copy verified answers? {#cross-same-weights-privileged-view}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Conditions differ. The student only reads the question and generates its own prefix; the training teacher reads a verified answer before scoring that prefix. Supervision targets an unprivileged student. MOPD instead uses independent domain teachers. Neither can feed training answers into formal student prediction.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: A teacher can know the solution while evaluating the student's next step, but giving it to the student changes the task.

    Sources: [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md) · [MOPD](../../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en.md)

### Can token teacher routing average same-ID logits from different tokenizers? {#cross-mixture-events-before-probabilities}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Soft routing mixes probabilities over identical events, not generally logits or log-probabilities. Different tokenizers can assign the same ID to different text. CSD aligns textual events and preserves REST mass first. Fine-grained routing cannot fix incompatible event identity.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Token 17 could be a whole word for one teacher and a fragment for the student; shared numbering does not make them the same event.

    Sources: [Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.21234-token-teacher-selection/README-en.md) · [CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer](../../../../post-training/2610.28895-csd/README-en.md) · [MOPD](../../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en.md)

### Does SPOD freeze a successful episode when the teacher disfavors one action? {#cross-success-not-whole-episode-freeze}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Success and raw complete-action probabilities identify qualifying decisions; only there does SPOD remove distillation and add a soft floor. Other decisions keep learning. MOPD and OPSD do not automatically protect this behavior.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: If step two works despite being unusual, protecting it need not discard useful corrections to steps one and three.

    Sources: [Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.25034-spod/README-en.md) · [MOPD](../../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en.md) · [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md)

### Does giving an OPSD teacher more visual evidence prove its corrections are visual? {#cross-privilege-not-visual-attribution}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Language priors, style, and prior prefix mistakes can also change. VAD contrasts evidence presence and removal with the same teacher and student prefix, then projects the original correction. Privileged inputs alone do not supply attribution, and the local proxy is not genuine visual attribution.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: A crop might cause shorter phrasing even if brevity is not supported by the image; compare views to distinguish shared changes.

    Sources: [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md) · [VAD](../../../../post-training/2607.28590-vad/README-en.md)
